evals.prompt: I have an Excel file with feature requirements for multiple portable AC models (PSS fixed-frequency, PDS fixed-frequency, PDS inverter). Each row contains a feature name, feature description, and which models support it. The data is complete but unstructured — the same feature like temperature control is described differently across rows, and there's no consistent grouping. Please help me organize this into a standardized PRD with L1-L3 hierarchy, feature matrix with PK product comparison, and appendices.
evals.expected_output: A complete L1-L3 structured PRD with feature overview, function matrix organized by domain, PK product comparison table using ✔/✘ markers, interconnection/exclusion rules, and appendices.

assertions.name: l1_l3_structure
assertions.description: Output follows a clear L1 (functional domain) → L2 (functional group) → L3 (specific feature) three-level hierarchy

assertions.name: pk_comparison_matrix
assertions.description: Multi-product features use ✔/✘ comparison matrix with differences noted in remarks column

assertions.name: complete_sections
assertions.description: PRD includes core sections: product overview, feature matrix, interconnection/exclusion rules, fault codes & messaging, certification strategy, and appendices

assertions.name: no_copy_paste
assertions.description: Output is not a copy-paste of raw input — includes merged common items and extracted shared rules

evals.prompt: Here's a PRD template from our existing product (Matter portable AC PSL/PDL/PDM). I need you to write a PRD for a new product (PSS/PDS series) based on this template structure. The new product has similar features but with some differences: the default cooling temperature is 16°C instead of 18°C, it supports heating mode up to 30°C, and there's a new Bluetooth generator (ICA) feature only on the inverter model. Please follow the template's section structure, table format, and appendix style.
evals.expected_output: A PRD for the new PSS/PDS products that mirrors the template's structure (sections, table formats, appendix style) while correctly incorporating the new product's unique features and differences.

assertions.name: template_structure_match
assertions.description: Section structure, table format, and appendix style match the provided template

assertions.name: new_product_content
assertions.description: Content reflects the new PSS/PDS product features, not copied from the template's original product

assertions.name: capability_extension
assertions.description: New capabilities not in the template (e.g., Bluetooth generator/ICA, updated temperature ranges) are correctly added and documented

assertions.name: appendix_consistent
assertions.description: Appendices (interconnection/exclusion rules, power-on/off state tables) follow the template's format and style

evals.prompt: I'm giving you a messy set of feature descriptions for a commercial air conditioning product. The same temperature control logic is described in 3 different places with slightly different numbers (16-32°C in one place, 18-32°C in another, 16-30°C in a third). Wind speed settings are mentioned under both 'control' and 'mode' sections with conflicting defaults. Some rules contradict each other — e.g., one section says auto mode supports temperature adjustment, another says it doesn't. The PK product names are mixed with feature descriptions. Please help me reorganize this into a clean, standardized PRD.
evals.expected_output: A reorganized, deduplicated PRD with resolved conflicts, extracted common rules, and a clear logical structure without contradictions.

assertions.name: duplicate_merged
assertions.description: Repeated feature descriptions (e.g., temperature logic mentioned 3 times) are merged into a single, unified description

assertions.name: conflicts_resolved
assertions.description: Conflicting rules (e.g., different temperature ranges, contradictory auto mode behavior) are identified and either resolved or explicitly marked for confirmation

assertions.name: common_rules_extracted
assertions.description: Features common across multiple products are extracted into independent modules rather than repeated under each product

assertions.name: logical_clarity
assertions.description: Output is logically consistent — no contradictory statements remain in the final PRD

evals.prompt: I have a simple feature checklist for a smart air conditioning product: 'needs network pairing (scan QR code), supports cooling/heating/dehumidification/fan/auto modes, temperature adjustment, wind speed control (low/medium/high/auto), swing on/off, countdown timer 0.5-24h, cloud scheduling with repeat patterns, device sharing (both WAN and Matter), offline alert, OTA upgrade, voice control via Google/Alexa.' That's all I have. Please expand this into a complete, detailed product requirements document with all necessary appendices.
evals.expected_output: A detailed, structured PRD that expands the simple checklist into a comprehensive document with multi-condition branching rules, interconnection/exclusion rules, fault code tables, message push specifications, and a functional index appendix.

assertions.name: functional_index
assertions.description: Output includes a functional quick-reference table or appendix mapping features to sections

assertions.name: multi_condition_rules
assertions.description: Feature descriptions include multi-condition branching (e.g., temperature/wind speed limits vary by mode — cooling vs. heating vs. dehumidification)

assertions.name: cross_reference_rules
assertions.description: Output includes interconnection/exclusion rules or a disabled-rules summary table (e.g., which buttons are invalid in which modes)

assertions.name: detail_richness
assertions.description: Each L3 feature includes specific parameters, ranges, default values, and exception handling — not just feature names

assertions.name: message_push_rules
assertions.description: Output includes fault codes, message severity levels, and push notification rules (if applicable to the product type)
